I want to get off social media, or at least reduce my presence, and I thought I'd get all my data. This is a post about Instagram.

<!--more-->

*I want to get off social media, or at least reduce my presence, and I thought I'd get all my data. This is a post about Instagram.*

*First I did this: <https://help.instagram.com/7130835797039956/>*

*The download is a zip file with supposedly all of your information. It does not provide everything. Some of the data is limited to the previous week, some is limited to when Instagram features came in and out of use.*

*Should I start with the file named `start_here.html`? Yes. It provides a good structure for this post as well. I'm going to include all the categories and lots of information in an anonymous way.*

[start_here.html](start_here.html)

## **About your download**

Your information can be found in the HTML files in this download. We recommend viewing your download on a desktop device in order to use these links to navigate to your information. The links don't work on mobile devices.

On a mobile device, use the folders in the download to go to the HTML files. Each type of information is stored in its own HTML file and can be viewed by opening the file.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### **Avatars Store**

Info associated with Avatars Store, such as your personal avatar, and avatar items that you purchased or added to your wardrobe

You have no data in this section

### **Shopping**

Information about your shopping activity on Instagram

You have no data in this section

### **Comments**

Comments you've posted on your own content or on other people's content

[Post comments](your_instagram_activity/comments/post_comments_1.html)

[Reels Comments](your_instagram_activity/comments/reels_comments.html)

[Comments reported](your_instagram_activity/comments/comments_reported.html)

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(rvest)

fldr = './instagram-nmoorenz-2026-03-16/'

month_df = function(full_file_name, df_type) {
    read_html(x = full_file_name) |> 
    html_elements("table") |> 
    html_text() |> 
    str_extract('(?<=Time).+') |> 
    mdy_hm() |> 
    round_date(unit="month") |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    mutate(type = df_type) |> 
    rename(month = value)
}

post_comments = month_df(paste0(fldr, "your_instagram_activity/comments/post_comments_1.html"), 'Post Comments')
    
comments_reported = month_df(paste0(fldr, "your_instagram_activity/comments/comments_reported.html"), 'Comments Reported')

reels_comments = month_df(paste0(fldr, "your_instagram_activity/comments/reels_comments.html"), 'Reels Comments')

df_comments = rbind(post_comments, comments_reported, reels_comments) |> 
    count(month, type)

ggplot(df_comments, aes(x=month, y=n, fill=type)) + 
    geom_col() +
    ggtitle('Comments over time')


```

### **Likes**

Content you've liked

[Liked comments](your_instagram_activity/likes/liked_comments.html)

[Liked posts](your_instagram_activity/likes/liked_posts.html)

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# every fifth element
date_seq = c(rep(FALSE,4),TRUE)

liked_comments = read_html(x = paste0(fldr, "your_instagram_activity/likes/liked_comments.html")) |> 
    html_elements("main") |> 
    html_elements("div") |> 
    _[date_seq] |> 
    html_text() |> 
    mdy_hm() |> 
    round_date(unit="month") |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    rename(month = value) |> 
    mutate(type = 'Liked Comments')

liked_posts = read_html(x = paste0(fldr, "your_instagram_activity/likes/liked_posts.html")) |> 
    html_elements("div._3-94") |> 
    html_text() |> 
    mdy_hm() |> 
    round_date(unit="month") |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    rename(month = value) |> 
    mutate(type = 'Liked Posts')


df_likes = rbind(liked_comments, liked_posts) |> 
    count(month, type)

ggplot(df_likes, aes(x=month, y=n, fill=type)) + 
    geom_col() +
    ggtitle('Likes over time')



```

### **Story interactions**

Interactions that you've had with other people's stories

[Quizzes](your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/quizzes.html) *(8 interactions from 2019 to 2023)*

[Question Music Response](your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/question_music_response.html) *(5 interactions from 2020 to 2021)*

[Emoji sliders](your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/emoji_sliders.html) *(15 interactions from 2018 to 2021, 11 of which were 100)*

[Polls](your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/polls.html) *(Chart below)*

[Questions](your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/questions.html) *(Chart below)*

[Story Reaction Sticker Reactions](your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/story_reaction_sticker_reactions.html) *(2 from 2023)*

[Story likes](your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/story_likes.html) *(Chart below)*

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

month_df = function(filename, df_type, seq_num) {
    # create sequence for entries to keep
    date_seq = c(rep(FALSE,seq_num-1),TRUE)
    
    # last thing gets returned
    read_html(x = filename) |> 
    html_elements("main") |> 
    html_elements("div") |> 
    _[date_seq] |> 
    html_text() |> 
    mdy_hm() |> 
    round_date(unit="month") |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    rename(month = value) |> 
    mutate(type = df_type)
}

polls = month_df(paste0(fldr, "your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/polls.html"), "Polls", 6) 

questions = month_df(paste0(fldr, "your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/questions.html"), "Questions", 4)

story_likes = month_df(paste0(fldr, "your_instagram_activity/story_interactions/story_likes.html"), "Story Likes", 4)

df_stories = rbind(polls, questions, story_likes) |> 
    count(month, type)

ggplot(df_stories, aes(x=month, y=n, fill=type)) + 
    geom_col() +
    ggtitle('Stories, Questions, and Polls')


```

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

month_df = function(filename, df_type, seq_num) {
    # create sequence for entries to keep
    date_seq = c(rep(FALSE,seq_num-1),TRUE)
    
    # last thing gets returned
    read_html(x = filename) |> 
    html_elements("main") |> 
    html_elements("div") |> 
    _[date_seq] |> 
    html_text() |> 
    mdy_hm() |> 
    round_date(unit="month") |> 
    as_tibble() |> 
    rename(month = value) |> 
    mutate(type = df_type)
}

followers = month_df(paste0(fldr, "connections/followers_and_following/followers_1.html"), "Followers", 5) 

following = month_df(paste0(fldr, "connections/followers_and_following/following.html"), "Following", 5)

removed_suggestions = month_df(paste0(fldr, "connections/followers_and_following/removed_suggestions.html"), "Removed Suggestions", 5)

df_follow = rbind(followers, following, removed_suggestions) |> 
    count(month, type)

ggplot(df_follow, aes(x=month, y=n, fill=type)) + 
    geom_col() +
    ggtitle('Followers, Following, Suggestions (since 2016)')

```

When you choose to allow link history, website links for your recent in-app browsing activity are saved and this information may be used to improve your ads across Meta technologies. When you choose to not allow link history, your in-app browsing activity won't be saved or used to improve your ads. You can manage your link history settings from your in-app browser settings at any time
